Figure 2.9: The Slider Designer makes simple to define your code and link it to an underlying variable.

You will see the note frequently in the code as a reminder that can be cut out for easy reading.

Aside from the plug-in functions we discussed in Chapter 2, you will see more commented areas of code. In the first part // Add your code: you can add variables or function definitions just like you would in a .h file. Try to keep your code in the denoted area to make it easier to find and read. The area below says:

// ADDED BY RACKAFX -- DO NOT EDIT THIS CODE!!!
This is very important--you will see your important variable m_dVolume declared in this area. This is the portion of the .h file that RackAFX modifies when you add, edit, or delete controls from your. It is imperative that let RackAFX maintain this path of the C++ code. There are other properties of code in the .cpp file that have similar warnings and interesting hex symbols (0x1A7F, c....)—do not edit the code contained between the hex codes or commented areas. RackAFX writes C++ code for you. You will have to be careful not to alter the RackAFX C++ code in any way.
